Fauvism

Color set free — the Paris “wild beasts” of 1905 who painted green skies and red trees, and let emotion outrank accuracy.

Fauvism — you are hereBauhausMid-Century Modern
1

Where it comes from

Paris, the Salon d'Automne of 1905. Henri Matisse, André Derain and Maurice de Vlaminck hung canvases built from raw, unmixed color — a portrait with a green stripe down its face, a London river in emerald and vermilion. Critic Louis Vauxcelles, finding a tame Renaissance-style statue stranded among them, joked it was “Donatello among the wild beasts” — les fauves. The name stuck; the insult became a banner.

The movement burned bright and short — roughly 1905 to 1908 — but it permanently changed what color is allowed to do. Every expressive palette since, from expressionism to the modern web, walks through the door the Fauves kicked open.

2

Core principles

Color is emotion, not description

A face can be green if green is what the feeling needs. Color answers to the painter’s inner weather, not to the object in front of him.

Straight from the tube

Unmixed, saturated pigment laid down in bold strokes and flat slabs — the paint’s rawness is part of the meaning.

Clash on purpose

Complementaries at full strength, side by side: vermilion against emerald, ultramarine against orange. The vibration between them is the picture’s electricity.

Simplify the drawing

Forms are reduced to essentials — a tree becomes a green flame — so nothing competes with the color doing the talking.

4

Type & shape

Aa
ABCDEFGHIJKLM abcdefghjklm 0123456789

The Fauves were painters, not type designers — they left no house typeface, so their lettering follows the paint: heavy, hand-cut, poster-bold, the way Matisse would later letter his cut-paper books. On a website that means display type shouts from inside color blocks (the specimen is Archivo Black), while body text must be kept calm and parked on the deep ground or cream — the one place Fauvism is not allowed to improvise.

6

What it would mean for Peptopia

The feel: Mediterranean noon with the volume turned up: sun-drunk, joyful, a little dangerous. Nothing muted, nothing apologetic — a page that feels painted this morning.

  • Highest energy of the three, by a mile. The bar, the Arboretum and the kratom guides would feel painted, alive, unmistakably yours.
  • Text needs protection. Clashing saturated fields are glorious on cards but hostile to paragraphs — body text lives on Deep Ground or cream, always. That rule is what makes the style survivable.
  • The glass icons fight it. Holographic discs on painted slabs look pasted; the family would need painted rims and flatter discs — the brush icon already leans this way.
  • Best for joy, worst for calm. A mental-health portal in full Fauve would need the volume knob Matisse himself used: wild panels, quiet reading rooms.
